messages:
maya: Heads up — provisioning a new inference-heavy GKE cluster in asia-south1. Running into pod IP exhaustion on the shared-VPC when scaling GPU nodepools. Need guidance on expanding the pod secondary range + accelerator quota increases.

jon: Which project/subnet are we talking about? Also list exact accelerator types and counts you want to request.

maya: project: redwood-prod-asia
current pod secondary range: 10.40.0.0/22 (pods)
service secondary range: 10.41.0.0/24
scale target: ~1500 pods across GPU nodepools (canaries + prod)
autoscaler target: ~80 GPU nodes (mix of A100 80GB + A10)
quota ask: A100-80GB: +60 (target total 80), A10: +120

priya: FYI a /22 is ~1024 addresses — not enough for 1500 pods. Recommend at least /20 (~4096) for headroom. Confirm services and pods use separate secondary ranges. If shared-VPC owners disallow expansion we can add a second pod secondary range and map new nodepools to it. Also watch route table capacity in the shared-VPC (many nodepools -> many routes).

maya: We're also getting route capacity warnings from the shared-VPC when adding larger nodepools. Are there route quota increases we should request besides the subnet expansion?

jon: I'll open the support/quota cases. Quick checks you can run locally: 
```
gcloud compute networks subnets describe asia-south1-subnet --region=asia-south1 --project=redwood-shared-vpc --format="table(name,secondaryIpRanges)"
gcloud compute project-info describe --project=redwood-prod-asia --format="json(quotas)"
```

gcp-quota-bot: To request accelerator quota increases open https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/quotas and filter for the accelerator types (Accelerator (A100) etc). For subnet secondary-range expansion file a support case and cc the shared-VPC owners.

rory: Ops notes / suggestions:
- If expansion is denied: create an additional pod secondary range and update new GPU nodepools to use that range.
- Avoid drastically lowering max-pods-per-node (it increases node count and route churn).
- Configure cluster-autoscaler maxNodes for GPU nodepools so autoscaler can't overshoot IP capacity.
- Preflight script to check free IPs before a large scale-up: 
```
# inspect subnet secondary ranges
gcloud compute networks subnets describe asia-south1-subnet --region=asia-south1 --project=redwood-shared-vpc --format="json(secondaryIpRanges)"
# or list addresses (if you maintain reserved addresses for pod ranges)
gcloud compute addresses list --project=redwood-shared-vpc --filter="region:(asia-south1) name~pod-range" --format="value(address)"
```

aisha: Cost note: 80 A100 reserved is a large commitment. Suggest staged approach: start with small canary (8 A100 + 12 A10, mix spot/on-demand) for 2 weeks, collect utilization and perf data, then scale to 24 A100 + 40 A10 before moving to a reserved commit (6-12 months). Please provide utilization targets before we commit spend.

maya: Canary plan (tentative): create tainted GPU nodepool(s) for inference, set max-pods-per-node=50 for GPU nodes, start with 8 A100 dedicated nodes + 12 A10 spot nodes. Monitor: IP allocation, pod density, eviction/ooms, autoscaler events, and latency P95.

jon: Tickets opened: CLOUD-9017 (accelerator quota request for project=redwood-prod-asia), NET-3178 (shared-vpc subnet secondary-range expansion request). Linking both to infra-ops board; will update threads when support replies.

maya: Checklist: 
- [ ] CLOUD-9017 quota approval
- [ ] NET-3178 subnet expansion or new pod-secondary-range added
- [ ] nodepool creation with taints + maxPods=50
- [ ] canary run (8 A100 + 12 A10) + monitoring dashboards (ip-usage, pod density, autoscaler)
- [ ] cost sim for reserved commit and utilization targets

jon: I'll follow up as soon as support responds to the cases. :thumbsup:
